description:
## What breaks

A guard helper whose arity exceeds the calling clause's arity aborts the interpreter and works on the other two doors.

```
fn ordered?(a, b, c), do: a <= b and b <= c
fn kind(x, y) when ordered?(0, x, y), do: :rising
fn kind(_x, _y), do: :other
```

- `fz2 interp` -> `fz2 interp: backend clause dispatch required omitted semantic input 2` (a bare string, no diagnostic, no span)
- `fz2 run` -> correct
- `fz2 build` -> correct

Arity is the whole trigger; literal arguments are irrelevant. A helper called with only variables still breaks when it is wider (`fn three?(a,b,c)` called from `fn kind(x, y) when three?(x, y, x)`), and a helper called with a literal is fine when it is not (`fn gt?(lo, x)` called from `fn kind(a, _b) when gt?(0, a)`).

## Why

A reified helper is a `PatternGuardExpr::Dispatch` holding a nested plan whose subjects, pins and clause bodies are numbered `0..helper arity`. Both evaluators feed that plan exclusively from the `inputs` vector -- `ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs` executes it against `&values`, `jobs/native.rs` against `input_vars` -- so the argument list is the only bridge between the two index spaces.

`collect_guard_expr_inputs` (src/compiler2/artifact.rs) crossed them anyway: after collecting `inputs` against the caller's plan it also walked `dispatch.bodies` and `dispatch.plan.graph` and wrote *those* ordinals into the same set. `band/1` calling a 3-input helper therefore reported required inputs `{0, 1, 2}` for a plan with `input_count == 1`.

The doors then diverge on the impossible demand rather than on the guard:

- src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs:857 iterates its own semantic inputs and asks `required_inputs.contains(&i)`, so an out-of-range ordinal is simply never visited.
- src/ir_interp/backend.rs:605 iterates `required_inputs` and indexes into the call's arguments, so the ordinal is `None` and the call aborts.

## Fix

`collect_guard_expr_inputs` collects the argument expressions only. That is complete: every caller input a guard can reach flows through one of them.

`required_dispatch_input_ordinals` now asserts every ordinal it returns is below `plan.input_count`. An ordinal outside a plan's own input space is not a conservative over-approximation -- a backend may pass any non-required input as nil -- so it is a demand no caller can meet, and the assertion keeps that failure at the plan that produced it instead of at whichever door reads it first.

## Tests

- `fixtures2/behavior/guard_helper_wider_than_caller.fz` -- in-language assertions, all four paths.
- `compiler2_entry_dispatch_requires_only_its_own_inputs_when_a_helper_is_wider` -- pins `required_dispatch_input_ordinals` at `{0}` for `band/1`. Proven fail-at-HEAD: `{2, 0, 1}` vs `{0}`.
title: [BUG] A guard helper wider than its caller leaks its own input ordinals into the caller's dispatch demands
